x: We congratulate Birchfield upon scoring one over us; and both teams were delighted with the match—and, may it be said, are eager for the next. Jim Ginty, of ours, led the field home in 14 min. 43 sec., and Ring and Rice did well to finish third and fourth.
In the absence of Rice the Two Miles went to Hunter in 9.20, with veteran McCluskey doing 9.25. The High Jump and Pole Vault went at 6ft. 6in. and 14ft. respectively.

YOUTHS.—1, Maclean, 26.22; 2, Adams, 26.30; 3, Godfrey, 26.35; 5, Simpson, 26.50; 8, Greene, 26.58; 9, Courtney, 27.10; 13, Cornell, 27.58; 15, Rice, 28.0; 16, Butt, 28.20; 19, Udall, 28.41; 21, Macklin, 29.10; 22, Jones, 33.30.

Junior—6, Maclean, 29.32; 14, Courtney, 30.48; 26, Briggs, 32.04; 29, Fadden, 32.26; 32, Godfrey, 32.37; 36, Paterson, 33.01; 40, Henn, 33.27; 41, Stearman, 33[illegible]27; 42, Rice, 33.41; 46, Mitchell, 34.02.
The winner on this occasion-Les Cohen, followed by Footer, Jack Flower, Duffett, Penny, Allum, Rice, Pyer, with, needless to say, a Belgrave team win of convincing proportions.

Our next man was Wally Bayliss (9th) who had run a splendid race, then came Rice (a disappointment this - 16th) and Buckingham completed our scoring four who are to be congratulated on finishing 3rd in the team race - to St.
Our scorers were Penny (3rd), Duffett(4th), Mitchell (5th), Cook (7th), Footer (9th) and Rice (15th). South London Harriers (120) were second and Mitcham A.C.
The Captain that day was Bert Footer and the rest of the team were Allum, Carter, Flower, Ginty, Parker, Patience; Shaw, Ring, Rice, Shields and Taylor.
